html:
The second of the three great tragic poets of Athens, born around 497 BCE at Colonus, just outside the city. He wrote about 120 plays and won more first prizes than any other tragedian; he is said never to have come last.

Seven of his plays survive whole, including:

  • Antigone, about a woman who buries her brother against the king's order
  • Oedipus Rex, about a king who learns he killed his father and married his mother
  • Electra and Oedipus at Colonus

Aristotle held up Oedipus Rex as the model tragedy. Sophocles added a third actor and painted scenery, and he gave more weight to individual characters than Aeschylus had.

He also served the city, as a treasurer of the Delian League and as a general alongside Pericles in the war against Samos in 441 to 440 BCE. He lived through the whole golden age of Athens and died in 406 BCE, months after Euripides.
